questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never touch the operator.
Sit as far back on their seat as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a passenger, tell them to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When turning, it is important to:

options.text: Look straight ahead.
Slow down after starting into the turn.
Reduce your speed coming out of the turn.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet must have all of the following, except:

options.text: An impact-resistant outer shell.
An impact-absorbing inner liner.
A chinstrap retention system.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they wear:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Shoes should have low heels to avoid catching on foot pegs. Leather gloves or gloves made of durable material protect your hands and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Check your mirrors especially:

options.text: On long trips.
When riding through an intersection.
When following a vehicle.
Before slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before stopping, changing lanes, and slowing down.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When there are hazards on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep going straight. If you need to brake, use only the brake for the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Adjust your lane position as conditions change.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight for better visibility.
Follow other vehicles closely so you can see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Always adjust your lane position as conditions change, especially at night. Use safe riding techniques when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
Prevent brakes from activating on dry roads.
Apply brakes automatically.
Warn you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during emergency braking. It works when you apply maximum pressure to both the front and rear brake controls. If sensors detect a wheel locking up, the system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep your brakes working at their best.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
Speed up before shifting to a lower gear.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you that you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, you must be going slow enough to do it safely. If you shift too fast, the motorcycle may jerk and the rear wheel may skid. Use your brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: You should check traffic behind your motorcycle especially:

options.text: Before starting into a curve.
When approaching an intersection.
When carrying a passenger.
Before slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you slow down. Drivers behind you may not expect you to slow down or may not see that you are slowing down.

questions.question: It is recommended that a motorcyclist:

options.text: Shift gears while turning.
Shift gears before turning.
Change speed suddenly while turning.
Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you need to stop quickly on a wet surface. You can safely use the front brake on a wet surface if you apply it slowly to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Decrease the space between you and the vehicle ahead.
Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.
Ride faster than usual.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark. Slow down and increase your following distance at night. Use your high beam any time you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious.
Prevents you from changing direction.
Will usually fix itself.
Is only a problem if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents you from changing direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash or injury. Too much brake pressure can lock the rear wheel. Once the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean your weight forward and down. Pull to the side of the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: If the chain or belt of your motorcycle breaks, you will:

options.text: Get a sudden boost of power to the rear wheel.
Lose power to the rear wheel suddenly.
Lose power to the front wheel suddenly.
Get a sudden boost of power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose power to the rear wheel suddenly.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, you will lose power to the rear wheel right away.

questions.question: What should you do to maintain control while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright without leaning.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look ahead by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean the motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: During acceleration, a sidecar attached to a motorcycle will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
Vibrate uncontrollably.
Make acceleration feel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is a heavy mass attached to the motorcycle with no power of its own. Due to its weight and inertia, it will feel like it is lagging behind when you speed up.
